# Why Adámas is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Adámas** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Adámas appears in Greek myth not as a character but as a substance that binds, wounds, or armors the gods themselves. Its very hardness creates drama: what can hold an immortal must be stronger than the divine. Hesiod (Theogony 161) says Gaia gave Kronos an adamantine sickle (ἅρπην ἀδάμαντος) with which to wound his father Ouranos.  The tool is decisive: only a substance harder than sky can wound the sky.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Adámas
- **ASCII form:** adamas
- **Meaning:** "Unbreakable; the adamant; the hardest substance; origin of "diamond""
- **Domain of influence:** Gem, Concept, Invincibility
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** ἀδάμας
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 5 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **ἀδάμας**. On the evidence, it means "Unbreakable; the adamant; the hardest substance; origin of "diamond"".

Strip **Adámas** to *adamas* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → á** — Acute on alpha: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Adámas** lives at [/sites/adamas/](/sites/adamas/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/adamas/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/adamas/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/adamas/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Adámas** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials** — The adamant stone; the literal etymon of the diamond trade.
- **Mining & Natural Resources** — Diamond is mined before it is set; the earth's hardest yield is his namesake stone.
- **Manufacturing, Craft & Automation** — Only divine smiths can work him; Hephaistos forged adamantine bonds to hold Prometheus.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
